thread:
kevin (support): FYI customer ACME reported repeated 504s from /v1/rerank this morning, p95 spiking from ~300ms to 8-12s during bursts. Ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/t/ACME-482

maria (eng-runtime): Thanks—do we have request_ids or example payloads? 504 suggests gateway timeout but could be backend cpu/queueing.

kevin (support): Sent their logs in the ticket, sample request_id 6f8a2c4b. They said their client retries aggressively. Payload includes 80 candidates and context length ~600 tokens.

sam (oncall): 80 candidates is high for rerank. Our rerank kernels scale approx O(n * embed_cost). Under high concurrency that can blow up latency. Any rate numbers from ACME?

kevin (support): They peaked at ~220 rps for rerank for ~30s window, 10 concurrent clients each retrying on 504s.

jordan (sre): :eyes: That sounds like a retry storm causing queue buildup at the gateway. Check gateway logs for 502/504 patterns around 1891234400-1891234600 and for upstream 5xx. Also check batch sizes in the runtime trace for the request_id.

maria (eng-runtime): Pulled traces for 6f8a2c4b — backend instances show long queuing before execution, worker CPU saturated on one pod. Runtime returned 200 from model server but gateway timed out after 10s waiting for response due to lack of available workers.

maria (eng-runtime): Repro plan I'm proposing: 1) synthetic load with same candidate counts (80) 2) ramp to 250rps for 1m 3) enable client retries to mimic storm. Use the following script:

```bash
# simplified repro using siege-style loop
for i in {1..500}; do
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"input": "search query","candidates": ['$(yes '"candidate"' | head -n 80 | paste -sd, -)']}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank &
  sleep 0.02
done
```

sam (oncall): Good. Also test with reduced candidate counts (16, 32) and with client-side jitter/backoff. We need to know if the runtime queuing is linear with candidates or if certain payload sizes trigger regressions.

jordan (sre): Observed gateway timeouts correlate with per-request serialized payload sizes > ~60KB. ACME payloads are around 72KB. Could be hitting nginx buffer or slow body parsing. I'll check reverse-proxy configs for proxy_read_timeout / client_body_buffer_size.

maria (eng-runtime): Action list: - eng-runtime to reproduce and gather flamegraphs (assign to maria) - eng-sre to validate gateway timeout/limits and adjust backpressure config (jordan) - support to advise ACME to lower candidate_count to 32 and enable exponential backoff (kevin)

kevin (support): I've communicated mitigations to ACME: reduce candidates + backoff + we'll pause aggressive retries. They asked for a timeline for a permanent fix.

maria (eng-runtime): Temporary mitigation options: 1) reject requests with candidate_count > 64 with 429 and a friendly message + Retry-After 2) enforce per-customer concurrency limit at gateway 3) increase model worker pool for the customer (Dedicated style)

jordan (sre): I'll open an incident PR with the nginx config diff and a short-term bump to proxy_read_timeout while we verify. Long-term we should add backpressure headers so clients can back off before hitting gateway timeout.

deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2026, linked to ticket ACME-482.

sam (oncall): Once eng-runtime posts repro results, we'll decide whether to ship a 429 guardrail or to tune infra. For now, recommend customer throttle and reduce candidate_count to 32.

kevin (support): Closing loop: ACME accepted the temporary guidance and will test reduced payloads today. Will update this thread after they report. :thumbsup:
